body.translated_text: The <s>vaitānika</s> (Śrauta ritual) rules having been stated, we shall now expound the <s>gṛhya</s> (domestic) rites.

The three <s>pākayajñas</s> (cooked offerings) are: <s>huta</s> (oblations offered in the fire), <s>prahuta</s> (offerings made without fire), and <s>brahmaṇi huta</s> (offerings made to <s>brāhmaṇas</s> at a meal).
And they cite the <s>ṛc</s> (Vedic verse): 'He who with the fuel-stick, he who with the oblation, he who with the <s>Veda</s>...'

Even one who faithfully offers the fuel-stick may think 'I am sacrificing with this.' 'Homage to him who by oblation, who by the <s>Veda</s>' — even through knowledge alone there is satisfaction. Seeing this, the <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage) declared:

'For the strong one, for the cattle-seeker, for the shining one, a <s>Dasma</s>-worthy word: sweeter than ghee and honey, you have spoken.' This word of mine is indeed sweeter than ghee and honey — may there be this satisfaction, this sweetness — thus he declares.

'O <s>Agni</s>, by the <s>ṛc</s>, we bring to you an oblation fashioned from the heart. May these be your bulls, oxen, and cows.' These indeed — the bulls, oxen, and cows — belong to one who studies this <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study of the Veda).

'He who with homage, with proper sacrifice' — indeed, through <s>namaskāra</s> (salutation) alone, the gods do not disregard homage. For in the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> text it is stated: 'Sacrifice is indeed homage.'
Then, in the evening and morning, one should offer the cooked <s>haviṣya</s> (oblation food) into the fire.

To the deities of the <s>Agnihotra</s>: to <s>Soma</s>, to <s>Vanaspati</s>, to <s>Agnīṣomau</s>, to <s>Indrāgnī</s>, to <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s> (Heaven and Earth), to <s>Dhanvantari</s>, to <s>Indra</s>, to the <s>Viśvedevas</s> (All-gods), and to <s>Brahman</s>.
With '<s>svāhā</s>' (hail!), then follows the offering of <s>bali</s> (food-offerings).
To these same deities, and to the waters, to herbs and trees, to the house, to the house-deities, and to the <s>Vāstu</s>-deities (deities of the dwelling-site).

To <s>Indra</s> and to <s>Indra</s>'s people, to <s>Yama</s> and to <s>Yama</s>'s people, to <s>Varuṇa</s> and to <s>Varuṇa</s>'s people, to <s>Soma</s> and to <s>Soma</s>'s people — in each direction.
To <s>Brahman</s> and to <s>Brahman</s>'s people — in the center.
To the <s>Viśvedevas</s> (All-gods) and to all beings, to the day-wanderers — during the day.
To the night-wanderers — at night.
To the <s>Rakṣas</s> (demons) — toward the north.
'<s>Svadhā</s> (hail) to the fathers!' — wearing the sacred thread in the <s>prācīnāvītī</s> (left-shoulder) manner, the remainder should be poured toward the south.

Now, wherever one is about to offer, one should smear and mark a level ground area of at least an arrow's length on all sides, drawing six lines running north, three at each end running east, and three in the middle. Having sprinkled it, having established the fire, having placed fuel on it, having swept around it, and having spread the <s>barhis</s> (sacred grass) — to the east, to the south, to the west, and to the north — with the tips pointing north, one should silently sprinkle around.
The purification of the <s>ājya</s> (clarified butter) is done with the two <s>pavitras</s> (purifying strainers).

Taking two <s>kuśa</s> (sacred grass) blades, each a span's length, with unbroken tips and without inner knots, held at their ends between the thumbs and little fingers with both palms turned upward — with the impelling of <s>Savitṛ</s>: 'Impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, I purify you with the unbroken purifier, with the rays of the sun' — one purifies eastward, once with the <s>mantra</s> and twice silently.
In <s>ājya</s> oblations, the strewing of <s>barhis</s> may be already done or freshly done.
Likewise the <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (shares of clarified butter for <s>Agni</s> and <s>Soma</s>) in the <s>pākayajñas</s>.
Except for the <s>brahmā</s> (priest's share), <s>Dhanvantari</s> offering, <s>yajña</s>-stake, and <s>śūlagava</s> (spit-ox) rites.
'To such-and-such a deity, <s>svāhā</s>!' — thus one should offer.
<s>Agni</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, and <s>Brahman</s> — when no specific deity is prescribed.
The <s>barhis</s> (sacred grass), fuel, <s>ājya</s> (clarified butter), and <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (oblation to <s>Agni</s> who makes the offering successful) — these should be for the same occasion.

On this, the following ritual verse is sung: 'Having assembled the <s>pākayajñas</s>, with one <s>ājya</s>, one <s>barhis</s>, one should make the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>, even when the deities are different.'

During the northern course of the sun, in the waxing fortnight, under an auspicious <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion): the <s>caula</s> (tonsure) ceremony, <s>upanayana</s> (initiation), <s>godāna</s> (shaving ceremony), and <s>vivāha</s> (marriage).
Some hold that marriage may be performed at any time.
Before these ceremonies, one should offer four oblations of <s>ājya</s> (clarified butter).
With the three verses beginning 'O <s>Agni</s>, you purify the life-spans,' and with '<s>Prajāpati</s>, none other than you...'
Or with the <s>Vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances: <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Svaḥ</s>).
Some say both combined.
Some say none at all.
'You are <s>Aryaman</s> when you are among maidens' — this is the fourth verse at the marriage.
'One should first examine the family, both on the mother's and father's side' — as stated previously.
One should give the maiden to a man of intelligence.
One should marry a maiden endowed with intelligence, beauty, virtue, and auspicious marks, and who is free from disease.

The marks being difficult to ascertain, having made eight balls of flour: '<s>Ṛta</s> (cosmic order) was born first; upon <s>ṛta</s>, truth is established. May this maiden who has been born, herein find her way. What is true, may that be seen.' Having consecrated the balls with this <s>mantra</s>, one should say to the maiden: 'Take one of these.'

If she takes one from a field with crops on both sides, one should know: 'Her progeny will be rich in food.' From a cow-pen: she will be rich in cattle. From the sacrificial altar with earth: she will possess Vedic splendor. From a lake with no drying up: she will be prosperous in all ways. From a gambling house: she will be a gambler. From a crossroads: she will have two husbands who go forth as wanderers. From a barren field: she will be unfruitful. From a cremation ground: she will cause her husband's death.

Having adorned the maiden, one should give her preceded by a water libation — this is the <s>Brāhma</s> form of marriage. The son born from such a marriage purifies twelve generations before and twelve after, on both sides.
If one gives her adorned during the performance of a Vedic sacrifice — that is the <s>Daiva</s> form. It purifies ten before and ten after, on both sides.
'Practice <s>dharma</s> together' — this is the <s>Prājāpatya</s> form. It purifies eight before and eight after, on both sides.
If one marries after giving a pair of cattle — that is the <s>Ārṣa</s> form. It purifies seven before and seven after, on both sides.
If one marries by mutual agreement — that is the <s>Gāndharva</s> form.
If one marries by winning over with wealth — that is the <s>Āsura</s> form.
If one carries off a maiden who is sleeping or distracted — that is the <s>Paiśāca</s> form.
If one carries off a weeping maiden from her weeping relatives, having struck and broken heads — that is the <s>Rākṣasa</s> form.
Now, the various customs of regions and villages — those should be followed in the marriage.
What is common to all, that we shall now state.

Having placed a grinding stone west of the fire and a water-pot to the northeast, while she holds on to it, having offered, standing, facing west, to her who sits facing east: 'I grasp your hand for good fortune' — he should grasp only the thumb, if he desires: 'May only sons be born to me.'
Only the fingers, if he desires daughters.
The hand up to the hair-tips, including the thumb, if he desires both.

Leading her around the fire and the water-pot three times clockwise, he recites: 'I am he, you are she; you are she, I am he. I am the sky, you are the earth; I am the <s>Sāman</s>, you are the <s>Ṛc</s>. Come, let us marry; let us beget offspring. Loving, radiant, well-disposed, may we live a hundred autumns.'
After each circumambulation, he makes her step onto the stone: 'Step upon this stone; be firm like a stone. Overcome those who oppose you; stand firm against adversaries.'
The bride's brother, or one standing in a brother's place, pours parched grain twice into the bride's joined hands.
Three times, according to the <s>Jāmadagnya</s> tradition.
The oblation is sprinkled over with ghee.
And the portion that falls off as well.
This is the rule for the offering portions.

'The maiden has worshipped the god <s>Aryaman</s> through <s>Agni</s>. May this god <s>Aryaman</s> release her from here, not from there. <s>Svāhā</s>!' 'The maiden has worshipped the god <s>Varuṇa</s> through <s>Agni</s>. May this god <s>Varuṇa</s> release her from here, not from there. <s>Svāhā</s>!' 'The maiden has worshipped the god <s>Pūṣan</s> through <s>Agni</s>. May this god <s>Pūṣan</s> release her from here, not from there. <s>Svāhā</s>!' — without interruption, from the joined hands she should offer as if with a ladle.
Without circumambulation, silently, a fourth time with the winnowing basket turned inward.
Some lead the bride around while pouring the parched grain at each turn; thus the last two oblations do not coincide.
Then he loosens her hair-knots, if they have been made, the woolen threads tied on either side of the hair-parting.
'I release you from the bonds of <s>Varuṇa</s>.'
The upper knot with the upper verse.

Then he makes her take seven steps toward the unconquered direction (northeast): 'For food, one step; for strength, two steps; for prosperity, three steps; for happiness, four steps; for offspring, five steps; for the seasons, six steps; be my companion with the seventh step. Be devoted to me. May we obtain many sons; may they reach old age.'
Bringing their heads close together, he sprinkles both with the water-pot.
That night she should stay in the house of an elderly <s>brāhmaṇī</s> (brāhmaṇa woman) whose husband and children are alive.
Having seen <s>Dhruva</s> (the Pole Star), <s>Arundhatī</s>, and the Seven <s>Ṛṣis</s> (sages), she should break her silence: 'May I live with my husband and obtain offspring.'
When a journey is at hand, with the verse 'May <s>Pūṣan</s> lead you hence, taking your hand,' he should make her mount the vehicle.
With the half-verse 'The stony one flows forth, brace yourselves,' he should have her board the boat.
She should disembark on the northern side.
When she weeps, [he recites] 'They weep for the living one.'
They lead the <s>vivāha</s> (wedding) fire in front, keeping it burning continuously.
At auspicious places, trees, and crossroads, he should mutter 'May they not find highwaymen.'
At each dwelling, with [the verse] 'Auspicious is this bride,' he should look at the onlookers.
With [the verse] 'Here may your beloved prosper with offspring,' he should have her enter the house.

Having piled up the <s>vivāha</s> (wedding) fire, spreading behind it a bull's hide with the neck facing east and the hair upward, when she is seated upon it and he has grasped her hand, he offers into the fire with the four verses beginning 'May <s>Prajāpati</s> generate offspring for us,' one oblation per verse. Having fed her curds with [the verse] 'May the <s>Viśvedevāḥ</s> unite,' he should have her pass it back, or he anoints her heart with the remainder of the <s>ājya</s> (clarified butter).

From that point onward, they should eat food without pungent seasoning or salt, observe <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy), sleep on the ground, adorning themselves properly, for three nights or twelve nights.
Or for a year — [then] a <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage) will be born, [so says the tradition].
Having fulfilled the vow, he should give a garment to the one who knows the <s>Sūryā</s> hymn for the bride.
And food to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>.
Then he should have a <s>svastyayana</s> (benediction) recited.
From the <s>pāṇigrahaṇa</s> (hand-grasping ceremony) onward, he should perform the <s>gṛhya</s> (domestic) rites himself, or his wife, or a son, or an unmarried girl, or a resident student.
He should always remain in a state of grace.
But if [the fire] should go out, some say the wife should fast.
The times of the kindling oblation of his <s>agnihotra</s> are explained by [the rules of] the <s>agnihotra</s> itself.
And the oblation material is the same, excluding meat.
But optionally, [one may offer] with rice, barley, or sesame.

In the evening he should offer with '<s>Agnaye</s> <s>svāhā</s>' (To <s>Agni</s>, hail!), in the morning with '<s>Sūryāya</s> <s>svāhā</s>' (To <s>Sūrya</s>, hail!); the second [oblation] at both times is [offered] silently.
Now [follows] the <s>pārvaṇa sthālīpāka</s> (new and full moon cooked offering).
For this, the fasting is [observed] on the new moon and full moon days.
And the tying together of the fuel and the <s>barhis</s> (sacrificial grass).
And the deities [are invoked] in a low voice, except for <s>Jāyā-Indra</s> and <s>Mahā-Indra</s>.
The other [offerings] are optional.

For each deity, he threshes out four handfuls [of grain], placing them between the purifying blades [of grass, saying] 'For you, O [deity], I thresh out what is pleasing,' for each deity respectively.
Then he sprinkles them as they have been threshed out, [saying] 'For you, O [deity], I sprinkle what is pleasing.'
Having husked [the grains] and broken them three times, he should cook them separately.
Or having combined them.
If he cooks them separately, having divided the rice grains, he should touch them [saying] 'This is for such [a deity], this is for such [a deity].'
But if he has combined them, he should offer the extracted portions.

Having basted the cooked oblations [with butter], having removed them to the north and placed them on the <s>barhis</s> (sacrificial grass), having basted the fuel, [he recites] 'This is your fuel, O <s>Jātavedas</s> (knower of all births), by this be kindled and increase; and being kindled, increase us with offspring, cattle, <s>brahmavarcas</s> (spiritual radiance), and food. Prosper us! <s>Svāhā</s>!'

Having silently poured the two <s>āghāra</s> (preliminary butter oblations), he should offer the two <s>ājyabhāga</s> (butter portions): '<s>Agnaye</s> <s>svāhā</s>' (To <s>Agni</s>, hail!) and '<s>Somāya</s> <s>svāhā</s>' (To <s>Soma</s>, hail!).
The one for <s>Agni</s> is to the north, the one for <s>Soma</s> is to the south.
For it is known: 'The two <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (butter portions) are indeed the two eyes of the sacrifice.'
Therefore, when a person sits facing west, the right eye is to the north and the left eye is to the south.
The main oblations [are offered] in the middle, or more toward the east; [they are placed] ending in the east, or ending in the north.
The <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (oblation for correct offering) is to the northeast.
He cuts off [a portion] from the middle and from the front half of the oblation.
According to those who hold five cuttings: from the middle, from the front half, and from the back half.
The <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> [portion is taken] from the northern half.
Here he does not baste the oblations again.

[He recites:] 'Whatever of this rite was done in excess, or whatever was done deficiently here — may <s>Agni</s> <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, the wise one, make all well-offered and well-sacrificed for me. To <s>Agni</s> <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s>, who makes well-offered and well-sacrificed, who brings to fulfillment the oblations of all expiations and desires, fulfill all desires for food. <s>Svāhā</s>!'
He should carry a full vessel to the <s>barhis</s> (sacrificial grass).
This is the <s>avabhṛtha</s> (concluding bath ritual).
This is the basic pattern for the <s>pākayajñas</s> (cooked-food sacrifices).
The remainder of the oblation is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee).
Now [follows] the <s>paśu-kalpa</s> (animal sacrifice procedure).

Having prepared a place for the <s>śāmitra</s> (slaughter fire) to the north of the [main] fire, having given the animal water to drink, having bathed it, having stationed it to the east facing west, having offered with the two [verses] beginning '<s>Agni</s> the messenger,' he should touch it from behind with a fresh branch bearing leaves, [saying] 'For you, O [deity], I consecrate what is pleasing.'
He sprinkles it from the east with waters mixed with rice and barley, [saying] 'For you, O [deity], I sprinkle what is pleasing.'
Having given it those [waters] to drink, he should pour the remainder along the right foreleg.
Having carried fire around it in the regular direction, they lead it northward.
Before it they carry a firebrand.
This becomes the <s>śāmitra</s> (slaughter fire).
The slaughterer grasps the animal along with the <s>vapā-śrapaṇī</s> (omentum-cooking vessels).
The sacrificer [grasps] the slaughterer.

Behind the <s>śāmitra</s> fire, [the animal is laid] with head to the east or head to the west, feet to the north. Having killed it, having placed grass below the navel, having cut out the <s>vapā</s> (omentum), having excised the <s>vapā</s>, having held it with the <s>vapā-śrapaṇī</s> (omentum vessels), having sprinkled it with water, having heated it at the <s>śāmitra</s> fire, having carried it past the [main] fire, sitting to the south, having cooked it, having circumambulated, he should offer it.
In this same fire they cook the <s>sthālīpāka</s> (cooked grain offering).
Having cut eleven portions from the animal from all its limbs, having cooked them at the <s>śāmitra</s> fire, having heated the heart on a spit, he should offer [them] before the <s>sthālīpāka</s>.
Or together with the cut portions.
Of each single cut portion, he cuts off two pieces each.
They carry about the heart-spit in the regular direction.
In the <s>caitya-yajña</s> (tree-shrine sacrifice), before the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>, he should offer a <s>bali</s> (food offering) to the sacred tree.
If indeed [the tree] is in a distant place, [he sends the offering] through a <s>palāśa</s> (Butea frondosa) branch as messenger.

With the verse 'Where you know, O lord of the forest,' having made two balls [of food] and placed them on the <s>vīvadha</s> (carrying pole), he should give them to the messenger, and tell him 'Carry this offering to that [tree].'
'This is for you' — [this is said] to the one who serves as messenger.
If there is danger on the way, [he should carry] any weapon whatsoever.
If there is a river that must be crossed by boat on the way, anything that can serve as a float should be used for crossing.
In the <s>Dhanvantari-yajña</s> (sacrifice to <s>Dhanvantari</s>), between the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> and the fire, he should offer a <s>bali</s> to the <s>purohita</s> (house priest's) fire.
In the <s>Upaniṣad</s> [section are taught]: <s>garbha-lambhana</s> (conception rite), <s>puṃsavana</s> (rite for begetting a male child), and the rite for preventing miscarriage.

If she does not conceive, in the third month of pregnancy, under the <s>Tiṣya</s> (Puṣya) asterism, having had her fast, he should feed her two <s>māṣa</s> beans and a barley grain in curds from a cow that has a calf of the same color, [mixed] with a handful of curds.
When asked 'What do you drink? What do you drink?' she should declare three times '<s>Puṃsavana</s>! <s>Puṃsavana</s>!'
Thus three handfuls [are administered].
Then, in the shadow of a round hut, he applies an undefeated herb into her right nostril.
Some [say the verse beginning] '<s>Prājāvat</s>' [and the verse] 'by two living sons.'
[He recites the verse:] 'Of <s>Prajāpati</s>: That which is placed in your heart, O <s>Susīmā</s>, within <s>Prajāpati</s> — I think I know that; may I not go to the evil of losing grandchildren.'
In the fourth month of pregnancy, [he performs] the <s>sīmanta-unnayana</s> (parting of the hair ceremony).
[It is performed] during the waxing fortnight, when the moon is conjoined with a masculine asterism.

Then, having piled up the fire, spreading behind it a bull's hide with the neck facing east and the hair upward, when she is seated upon it and he has grasped her hand, he offers with the two [verses] beginning '<s>Dhātā</s> gives to the generous one,' with the two [verses] beginning 'O <s>Rākā</s>, I,' and with [the verse] 'May this one not be harmed, O <s>Prajāpati</s>, no other than you.'

Then he parts her hair upward with an even number of <s>śalāṭu</s> (unripe fruits), a <s>grapsa</s> (porcupine quill), a <s>treṇī</s> (spindle-like) reed, and three bunches of <s>kuśa</s> grass, [reciting] '<s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Svaḥ</s>, <s>Om</s>' — three times.
Or four times.
Excluding the <s>gāthins</s> (chanters of gāthā verses), he instructs [two lute-players]: 'Sing of King <s>Soma</s>.'
'May King <s>Soma</s> protect our human offspring' — [this is the song about] the river near which they dwell.
And <s>brāhmaṇī</s> women who are elderly, whose husbands are living, and whose children are living — whatever they should prescribe, that they should do.
A bull is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee).

Before anyone else touches the newborn child, he should feed it <s>sarpis</s> (clarified butter) and honey, rubbed with gold, using a piece of gold, [reciting:] 'I give you this <s>Veda</s>, impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>, [consisting] of honey and ghee, of the generous ones. May you live long, protected by the gods, a hundred autumns in this world.'

Placing [his mouth] near the ears, he whispers the <s>medhā-janana</s> (intelligence-generating) [formula]: 'May god <s>Savitṛ</s> bestow upon you wisdom, may goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> [bestow] wisdom, may the two <s>Aśvin</s> gods, wearing lotus garlands, bestow wisdom upon you.'

He touches the shoulders [saying]: 'Be a stone, be an axe, be unpierceable gold. You are indeed the <s>Veda</s>, O son by name; live a hundred autumns.' [And the verse:] 'O <s>Indra</s>, bestow upon us the most excellent riches; grant [them], O bountiful one, O mighty one.'
And they should give the child a name that begins with a sonant, has a semivowel in the middle, ends with a <s>visarga</s> (aspiration), and consists of two syllables,
or four syllables.
Two syllables for one desiring stability, four syllables for one desiring <s>brahmavarcas</s> (spiritual radiance).
An even number of syllables for males, an odd number for females.
And one should consider the respectful greeting name; the mother and father should know it until the <s>upanayana</s> (initiation).

Having returned from a journey, the father, grasping the son's head, murmurs: 'From limb to limb you are born, from the heart you arise. You are indeed the self called son — live a hundred autumns,' smelling the crown of the head three times.
The same rite applies to a girl, but with the mantra recited silently.
In the sixth month, the <s>annaprāśana</s> (first feeding of solid food).
Goat meat for one desiring food,
partridge for one desiring <s>brahmavarcas</s> (spiritual radiance),
rice cooked in ghee for one desiring splendor.

He should feed the child food mixed with curds, honey, and ghee, reciting: 'O Lord of food, give us food that is free from disease and full of vigor. Carry forward the giver; bestow nourishment upon us, upon bipeds and quadrupeds.'
The same rite applies to a girl, but with the mantra recited silently.
In the third year, the <s>caula</s> (tonsure ceremony), or according to family custom.
To the north of the fire, he places separate dishes filled with rice, barley, beans, and sesame seeds.
Behind the one who is about to have the rite performed, seated in the mother's lap, there should be fresh cow dung in a new dish, and <s>śamī</s>-tree leaves placed alongside.
The mother's father, standing to the south, takes twenty-one bunches of <s>kuśa</s> grass.
Or the <s>Brahmā</s> priest may hold these.
Standing behind the one who is to have the rite performed, having mixed warm and cold water together, he says: 'Go forth with the warm water.'
Taking from those waters fresh butter or drops of curds, he moistens the head three times going clockwise, reciting: 'Let <s>Aditi</s> shave the hair; let the waters moisten him with splendor.'
On the right side of the hair, he places three bunches of <s>kuśa</s> grass with tips pointing inward, reciting: 'O herb, protect him.'
Pressing down with an iron razor, he recites: 'O knife, do not harm him.'

He cuts, reciting: 'With the razor by which <s>Savitṛ</s>, the knower, shaved <s>Soma</s> the king and <s>Varuṇa</s> — with that, O <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, shave this one, so that he may be long-lived, reaching old age.'
After each cutting, he hands the hair with <s>śamī</s>-leaves, tips pointing eastward, to the mother, who deposits them in the fresh cow dung.

'With the razor by which <s>Dhātṛ</s> shaved for the long life of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Agni</s>, and <s>Indra</s> — with that I shave you for long life, for good renown, for well-being' — the second time.
'With which one may live through more nights and long behold the sun — with that I shave you for long life, for good renown, for well-being' — the third time.
The fourth time, with all the mantras combined.
Likewise three times on the back of the head.
He should wipe the razor's edge clean, reciting: 'When with the razor, the well-adorned shaver, you shave the hair, purify the head — do not take away his life-span.'
He instructs the barber, while pouring warm and cold water for the purpose: 'Shave without cutting, skillfully.'
He should have the hair styled according to family custom.
The same rite applies to a girl, but with the mantras recited silently.
By this same procedure, the <s>godāna</s> (first shaving of the beard).
In the sixteenth year.
But where the word 'hair' occurs in the mantras, the word 'beard' should be substituted.
Here he moistens the beard.
'Purify the head and face — do not take away his life-span.'
He gives the instruction: 'Dispose of the hair, beard, body-hair, and nails by placing them in water.'
Having bathed, he should stand silent for the rest of the day in the teacher's presence, and then break silence by saying: 'I grant a gift.'
A pair of cattle, male and female, is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee).
One should prescribe a year of observance.
One should initiate a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> in the eighth year.
Or in the eighth year from conception.
A <s>Kṣatriya</s> in the eleventh year.
A <s>Vaiśya</s> in the twelfth year.
For a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the time has not passed until the sixteenth year.
For a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, until the twenty-second.
For a <s>Vaiśya</s>, until the twenty-fourth.
After that, they become persons who have lost the right to the <s>Sāvitrī</s> (fallen from investiture).
One should not initiate them, nor teach them, nor sacrifice for them, nor should people have dealings with them.
The boy, adorned, with his head properly prepared, clad in a fresh garment — in an antelope skin if a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, in a deer skin if a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, in a goat skin if a <s>Vaiśya</s>.
If they wear dyed garments: saffron for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, madder-red for a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, yellow for a <s>Vaiśya</s>.
Their girdles: of <s>muñja</s> grass for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, a bowstring for a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, wool for a <s>Vaiśya</s>.
Their staffs: of <s>palāśa</s> wood for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, of <s>udumbara</s> wood for a <s>Kṣatriya</s>, of <s>bilva</s> wood for a <s>Vaiśya</s>.
Or all types may be used for all.
Having performed the joint touching of the fire, after making oblations, the teacher stands to the north of the fire, facing east.
The student stands in front, facing west.

Filling both hands with water, reciting 'We choose that of <s>Savitṛ</s>,' he pours the full handful over the student's hands; then having sprinkled him, saying 'By the impulsion of the god <s>Savitṛ</s>, with the arms of the <s>Aśvins</s>, with the hands of <s>Pūṣan</s>, I grasp your hand, O so-and-so,' he should grasp his hand including the thumb.
'<s>Savitṛ</s> has grasped your hand, O so-and-so' — the second time.
'<s>Agni</s> is your teacher, O so-and-so' — the third time.
He should look at the sun. The teacher recites: 'O god <s>Savitṛ</s>, this is your <s>brahmacārin</s>; protect him; may he not die.'
'Whose <s>brahmacārin</s> are you? You are the <s>brahmacārin</s> of <s>Prāṇa</s>. Who entrusts you to whom? To whom do I deliver you?'
With the half-verse 'A youth, well-clad, girdled, has come,' he turns him around clockwise.
Placing both hands on his shoulders, he touches the region of the heart with the following verse.

Having swept around the fire, the <s>brahmacārin</s> should silently place a fuel-stick on the fire. It is taught: 'That which is silent belongs to <s>Prajāpati</s>; the <s>brahmacārin</s> belongs to <s>Prajāpati</s>.'

Some, however, do it with the mantra: 'I have brought a fuel-stick to <s>Agni</s>, to the great <s>Jātavedas</s>. By that, O <s>Agni</s>, may you increase through the fuel-stick; may we increase through sacred knowledge. <s>Svāhā</s>.'
Having placed the fuel-stick, he touches the fire and wipes his face three times, saying: 'I anoint myself with splendor.'
For it is taught: 'He thereby anoints himself with splendor indeed.'

Reciting: 'May <s>Agni</s> place in me intelligence, progeny, and radiance. May <s>Indra</s> place in me intelligence, progeny, and power. May <s>Sūrya</s> place in me intelligence, progeny, and brilliance. Whatever is your radiance, O <s>Agni</s>, may I become radiant thereby. Whatever is your splendor, O <s>Agni</s>, may I become splendid thereby. Whatever is your blazing force, O <s>Agni</s>, may I become blazing thereby' — having thus venerated the fire, bending the knee, he clasps the teacher's feet and says: 'Recite, sir; teach me the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, sir; repeat it.'
Grasping the student's hands with his garment and with his own hands, the teacher recites the <s>Sāvitrī</s> — first quarter by quarter, then half-verse by half-verse, then the whole.
He should have him recite it as many times as he is able.

He places his hand, fingers pointing upward, on the student's heart region, saying: 'I place your heart in my observance; may your mind follow my mind. May you rejoice in my speech with single-minded devotion. May <s>Bṛhaspati</s> yoke you to me.'
Having tied the girdle and given the staff, he should prescribe the <s>brahmacarya</s> (student's discipline).
'You are a <s>brahmacārin</s>. Sip water. Perform your duties. Do not sleep during the day. Devoted to the teacher, study the <s>Veda</s>.'
The <s>brahmacarya</s> for the <s>Veda</s> lasts twelve years, or until mastery of the text.
He should beg for alms in the evening and morning.
He should place a fuel-stick on the fire in the evening and morning.
He should first beg from a person who will not refuse,
or from a woman who will not refuse.
'Honored one, please give alms.'
Or this may serve as the <s>anupravacanīya</s> (post-instruction) offering formula.
He should report the alms to the teacher.
He should remain standing for the rest of the day.
After sunset, having cooked the <s>anupravacanīya</s> rice offering to <s>Brahman</s>, he should report it to the teacher.
The teacher, with the joint touching of the fire, offers oblations with the verse 'To the Lord of the assembly, the wondrous one.'
The second oblation with the <s>Sāvitrī</s>.
For whatever has not been mentioned above this point.
The third oblation to the <s>Ṛṣis</s> (sages).
The fourth is the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (making the oblation complete) offering.
Having fed the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, he should have the student recite the concluding formula of Vedic study.
After this, the <s>brahmacārin</s> should eat food without pungent spices or salt, sleep on the ground, for three nights, twelve nights, or a year.
For one who has completed the observances, he performs the <s>medhājanana</s> (rite for producing intelligence).

In a blameless direction, having the student circumambulate clockwise a <s>palāśa</s> tree with a single root, or a clump of <s>kuśa</s> grass in the absence of a <s>palāśa</s> tree, while pouring water from a pot three times around it, he has him recite: 'O <s>Suśravas</s>, you are of good hearing; as you are <s>Suśravas</s> of good hearing, so make me <s>Suśravas</s> of good hearing. As you are the guardian of the gods' sacrifice, so may I become the guardian of the <s>Veda</s> among men.'
By this, the instruction of observances from the shaving onward up to the girdle-tying is explained.
Thus for one who has not been previously initiated.
Now for one who has been previously initiated.
The shaving of hair may or may not be done.
And the prayer for the generation of intellect (<s>medhā-janana</s>).
The girdle-tying (<s>paridāna</s>) is without a specified mantra.
And the time.
The <s>Sāvitrī</s> verse is 'tat savitur vṛṇīmahe' (that of <s>Savitṛ</s> we choose).
He selects <s>ṛtvijas</s> (ritual priests) whose limbs are neither deficient nor excessive, who are as described earlier with respect to maternal and paternal lineage.
Some say he should select young <s>ṛtvijas</s>.
He selects first the <s>Brahman</s> priest, then the <s>Hotṛ</s>, then the <s>Adhvaryu</s>, then the <s>Udgātṛ</s>.
Or all those who officiate at <s>ahīna</s> (multi-day) and <s>ekāha</s> (one-day) sacrifices.
The <s>Kauṣītakins</s> enumerate a seventeenth, the <s>Sadasya</s> (assessor), saying he is the overseer of the rites.
Regarding that it has been said: 'whom the <s>ṛtvijas</s> arrange in many ways, like <s>Ṛbhus</s>.'
He selects the <s>Hotṛ</s> first.
'<s>Agni</s> is my <s>Hotṛ</s>, he is my <s>Hotṛ</s>; I choose you, so-and-so, as <s>Hotṛ</s>' — thus the <s>Hotṛ</s>.

'<s>Candramā</s> (the Moon) is my <s>Brahman</s>, he is my <s>Brahman</s>; I choose you, so-and-so, as <s>Brahman</s>' — thus the <s>Brahman</s> priest. '<s>Āditya</s> (the Sun) is my <s>Adhvaryu</s>' — thus the <s>Adhvaryu</s>.
'<s>Parjanya</s> (the Rain-god) is my <s>Udgātṛ</s>' — thus the <s>Udgātṛ</s>.
'The Waters are my <s>Hotra-āśaṃsinī</s> (assistant Hotṛ priests)' — thus the <s>Hotrakās</s>.
'The rays of the sun are my <s>Camasa-adhvaryus</s> (cup-bearing Adhvaryus)' — thus the <s>Camasa-adhvaryus</s>.
'Space is my <s>Sadasya</s> (assessor)' — thus the <s>Sadasya</s>.

The one selected should murmur: 'You have proclaimed greatness for me, you have proclaimed splendor for me, you have proclaimed fortune for me, you have proclaimed glory for me, you have proclaimed praise for me, you have proclaimed fitness for me, you have proclaimed enjoyment for me, you have proclaimed satisfaction for me, you have proclaimed everything for me.'
Having murmured, '<s>Agni</s> is your <s>Hotṛ</s>, he is your <s>Hotṛ</s>; I am your human <s>Hotṛ</s>' — thus the <s>Hotṛ</s> accepts.
'<s>Candramā</s> (the Moon) is your <s>Brahman</s>, he is your <s>Brahman</s>; the <s>Brahman</s> —'
Likewise the others, according to their respective assignments.
'May that protect me, may that enter me, by that may I prosper' — thus the one about to officiate.

The priestly office is to be refused for the following: one whose sacrifice has been abandoned, one with deficient <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (fees), one who is diseased, one who is ill, one seized by consumption, one instructed by an unworthy person, and one of impure birth.
Before the <s>Soma</s> purchase, one should inquire: 'What is the sacrifice? Who are the <s>ṛtvijas</s>? What is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (fee)?'
Association should be with auspicious persons.
They should not eat meat nor approach a woman until the completion of the rite.

Having offered an oblation of ghee in the <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s> (southern fire) with the verse 'etena agne brahmaṇā vāvṛdhasva' (By this prayer, O <s>Agni</s>, may you be strengthened), he should set out as needed.
Likewise one who has not established the sacred fires, using his domestic fire, with the verse 'imām agne śaraṇim mīmṛṣo naḥ' (O <s>Agni</s>, grant us this shelter).
Having selected the <s>ṛtvijas</s>, he should offer <s>Madhuparka</s> (the honey-drink hospitality).
To a <s>Snātaka</s> (one who has completed Vedic study) who has arrived.
And to a king.
And to the <s>Ācārya</s> (teacher), father-in-law, paternal uncle, and maternal uncle.
Having brought curds mixed with honey.
Or ghee mixed with honey, if curds are unavailable.
A grass seat, water for washing the feet, <s>arghya</s> (respectful water offering), water for sipping, the <s>Madhuparka</s>, and a cow — each of these they announce three times.
With the verse 'I am the highest among my kinsmen, like the sun among the lightnings; I stand upon this one, whoever may assail me' — he should sit on the grass seat with its tips pointing north.
Or stepping upon it.
He should have the feet washed.
He should offer the right foot first to a Brāhmaṇa.
The left foot to a Śūdra.
With feet washed, receiving the <s>arghya</s> in his joined palms, he then sips with the <s>ācamanīya</s> (sipping water), saying 'amṛta-upastaraṇam asi' (You are the underlayer of immortality).
He looks at the <s>Madhuparka</s> being brought, saying 'mitrasya tvā cakṣuṣā pratīkṣe' (I look upon you with the eye of <s>Mitra</s>).

With 'devasya tvā savituḥ prasave aśvinor bāhubhyām pūṣṇo hastābhyām pratigṛhṇāmi' (At the impulse of god <s>Savitṛ</s>, with the arms of the <s>Aśvins</s>, with the hands of <s>Pūṣan</s>, I receive you), he receives it in joined palms, places it in the left hand, examines it with the three verses beginning 'madhu vātā ṛtāyate' (The winds blow honey for the righteous), stirs it three times clockwise with the ring finger and thumb, and wipes it to the east saying 'vasavas tvā gāyatreṇa chandasā bhakṣayantu' (May the <s>Vasus</s> partake of you with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> meter).
'rudrās tvā traiṣṭubhena chandasā bhakṣayantu' (May the <s>Rudras</s> partake of you with the <s>Triṣṭubh</s> meter) — to the south.
'ādityās tvā jāgatena chandasā bhakṣayantu' (May the <s>Ādityas</s> partake of you with the <s>Jagatī</s> meter) — to the west.
'viśve tvā devā ānuṣṭubhena chandasā bhakṣayantu' (May all the <s>Devas</s> partake of you with the <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> meter) — to the north.
'bhūtebhyas tvā' (For the beings) — taking up three times from the middle.
He should eat the first portion saying 'virājo doho'si' (You are the milking of <s>Virāj</s>).
The second saying 'virājo doham aśīya' (May I partake of the milking of <s>Virāj</s>).
The third saying 'mayi dohaḥ padyāyai virājaḥ' (May the milking of <s>Virāj</s> settle in me).
Not all of it.
He should not eat to full satisfaction.
He should give the remainder (<s>ucchiṣṭa</s>) to a Brāhmaṇa to the north.
If no Brāhmaṇa is available, into water.
Or all of it.
Then he sips again with the <s>ācamanīya</s> water, saying 'amṛta-apidhānam asi' (You are the cover of immortality).
The second sipping with 'satyam yaśaḥ śrīr mayi śrīḥ śrayatām' (Truth, glory, prosperity — may prosperity take refuge in me).
To the one who has sipped the water, they announce the cow.
Having murmured 'hato me pāpmā pāpmā me hataḥ' (My sin is slain, slain is my sin), he should have it prepared, saying 'kṛṇuta' (do it).
Having murmured 'mātā rudrāṇām duhitā vasūnām' (Mother of the <s>Rudras</s>, daughter of the <s>Vasus</s>), he should have it released, saying 'utsṛjata' (release it).
The <s>Madhuparka</s> is never without meat.
On the full-moon day of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, the <s>Śrāvaṇa-karma</s> (Śrāvaṇa rite) is performed.
Having filled a new pot with unbroken parched grain (<s>saktus</s>), he places a ladle and a vessel for carrying the <s>bali</s> offering in a new sling.
Having made unbroken parched grains, he anoints half with ghee.

After sunset, having cooked a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (mess of cooked grain) and a single-plate cake (<s>ekakapāla puroḍāśa</s>), he offers with the four verses beginning 'agne naya supathā rāye asmān' (O <s>Agni</s>, lead us by the good path to prosperity), one oblation per verse, and the single-plate cake with his hand saying 'acyutāya bhaumāya svāhā' (To the Unfallen one, the Earthly one, <s>svāhā</s>).
He should be immersed in water, or with a ram-skin on his back.
With 'mā no agne avasṛjo aghāya' (O <s>Agni</s>, do not abandon us to evil), he makes an additional offering with the remains.
'śam no bhavantu vājino haviṣvāḥ' (May the vigorous ones bearing oblations be auspicious for us) — the anointed grains offered with joined palms.
The rest he should give to his companions.

Having filled a ladle with <s>saktus</s> from the pot, going out to the east, pouring water at a clean spot, and offering with 'sarva-deva-janebhyaḥ svāhā' (To all the divine beings, <s>svāhā</s>), he pays homage saying: 'The serpents that are terrestrial, those that are of the atmosphere, those that are celestial, those that belong to the directions — to them I have brought this <s>bali</s> offering, to them I present this <s>bali</s>.'

Going around clockwise, sitting behind the <s>bali</s>, he says: 'You are the serpent, the chief of serpents, their overlord; with food you protect humans, with cake you honor the serpents, with sacrifice you honor the gods. Those serpents that are in you, being in you, may they not harm us. O steadfast one, I entrust so-and-so to you.'
'O steadfast one, I entrust so-and-so to you, O steadfast one, I entrust so-and-so to you' — thus the companions, one after another.
'O steadfast one, I entrust myself to you' — himself last.
No one should pass between them until the entrusting is complete.
'sarpa-deva-janebhyaḥ svāhā' (To the divine serpent-beings, <s>svāhā</s>) — he should offer the <s>bali</s> evening and morning until the <s>Pratyavarohaṇa</s> (descent ceremony).
Some, having counted them, offer that many <s>bali</s> offerings all on that same day.
On the <s>Āśvayujī</s> (full moon of Āśvina), the <s>Āśvayujī-karma</s> (Āśvayujī rite).

Having adorned the dwelling, bathed and wearing clean garments, they should offer a <s>sthālīpāka</s> to <s>Paśupati</s>, making oblations with 'paśupataye śivāya śaṃkarāya pṛṣātakāya svāhā' (To <s>Paśupati</s>, to <s>Śiva</s>, to <s>Śaṃkara</s>, to <s>Pṛṣātaka</s>, <s>svāhā</s>).
He should offer the <s>pṛṣātaka</s> (speckled offering) with joined palms, saying 'May this be filled for me, may the full one not fail me — to <s>Pṛṣātaka</s>, <s>svāhā</s>.'

'sajūr ṛtubhiḥ sajūr vidhābhiḥ sajūr indrāgnibhyām svāhā' (Together with the seasons, together with the rules, together with <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s>, <s>svāhā</s>); 'sajūr ṛtubhiḥ sajūr vidhābhiḥ sajūr dyāvāpṛthivībhyām svāhā' (Together with the seasons, together with the rules, together with Heaven and Earth, <s>svāhā</s>) — this is the <s>Āgrayaṇa</s> (first-fruits) <s>sthālīpāka</s> for one who has established the sacred fires.
For one who has not established the sacred fires, it is offered in the household fire.
On the fourteenth day of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, the <s>Pratyavarohaṇa</s> (descent ceremony).
Or on the full-moon day.

Having renewed the dwelling with fresh plastering, spreading, and furnishing, after sunset they should offer a <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice oblation) with: 'apa śvetapadā jahi pūrveṇa ca apareṇa ca' (Strike away the white-footed one, both from the east and from the west); 'sapta ca vāruṇīr imāḥ sarvāś ca rāja-bāndhavīḥ svāhā' (And these seven belonging to <s>Varuṇa</s>, and all those connected with the king, <s>svāhā</s>); 'na vai śvetaś ca abhyāgāre ahir jaghāna kiṃcana, śvetāya vaidārvāya namaḥ svāhā' (The white serpent in the dwelling has harmed nothing — homage to the white <s>Vaidārva</s> serpent, <s>svāhā</s>).
There is no <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> oblation here.
Looking at the fire, he murmurs 'abhayam naḥ prājāpatyebhyo bhūyāt' (May there be freedom from fear for us from the creatures of <s>Prajāpati</s>).
He should meditate in his mind on winter, saying 'śivo naḥ sumanā bhava' (Be gracious and well-disposed to us).

Behind the fire, on a comfortable bed well-spread, having sat down and murmured 'syonā pṛthivi bhava' (O Earth, be pleasant), he should lie down together with his companions, with his head to the east, facing north.
The others according to available space.
The eldest or the next eldest adjacent.
Those who know the mantras should murmur them.
Pronouncing together 'ato devā avantu naḥ' (From here may the gods protect us), three times.
This same verse facing south, facing west, and facing north as the fourth.
Having pronounced together the solar hymns and benedictions, having prepared food, having fed the Brāhmaṇas, he should have a benediction recited.
On the eighth days of the four dark fortnights of <s>Hemanta</s> (early winter) and <s>Śiśira</s> (late winter), the <s>Aṣṭakā</s> (eighth-day) offerings are performed.
Or on one of them only.
On the preceding day, he should make offerings to the ancestors (<s>Pitṛs</s>).
Rice, <s>kṛsara</s> (a mixture of rice and sesame), and <s>pāyasa</s> (milk-rice).
Or cakes on four dishes.
Having offered with eight [repetitions] of '<s>udīratām avara utparāsaḥ</s>' (May the later and earlier [deceased ancestors] be uplifted), or with as many as one desires.
Then on the following day, the <s>Aṣṭakā</s> (eighth-day rite) [should be performed] with an animal and a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (cooked oblation).
He should also bring barley for the ox.
Or he should burn dry grass with fire.
'This is my <s>Aṣṭakā</s>' — thus.
But he should certainly not be without the <s>Aṣṭakā</s>.

Some call it dedicated to the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, some to <s>Agni</s>, some to <s>Sūrya</s>, some to <s>Prajāpati</s>, some [say] the deity is Night, some [say] the deity is the <s>Nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), some [say] the deity is the Seasons, some [say] the deity is the <s>Pitṛs</s> (ancestors), some [say] the deity is the Animals.

Having slaughtered the animal according to the animal-ritual procedure, omitting the sprinkling and the preliminary rites, cutting out the <s>vapā</s> (omentum), he should offer [saying]: '<s>vaha vapām Jātavedaḥ pitṛbhyo yatra etān vettha nihitān pakāre / medasaḥ kulyā upa enānt sravantu satyā etā āśiṣaḥ santu sarvāḥ svāhā</s>' (Carry the omentum, O <s>Jātavedas</s>, to the ancestors, where you know them to be established in the cooking-vessel. May streams of fat flow to them! May all these blessings be true! <s>Svāhā</s>!).

Then, for the portions and the <s>sthālīpāka</s> (cooked offering), [he recites] the two [verses] '<s>agne naya supathā rāye asmān</s>' (O <s>Agni</s>, lead us by the good path to prosperity). [Then]: '<s>grīṣmo hemanta ṛtavaḥ śivā no varṣāḥ śivā abhavā śaran naḥ / saṃvatsaro adhipatiḥ prāṇado no ahorātre kṛṇutām dūrgham āyuḥ svāhā</s>' (May summer, winter, and the seasons be auspicious for us, the rains auspicious, and autumn for us. May the Year, the overlord, be our life-giver; may day and night make for us long life! <s>Svāhā</s>!). '<s>śāntā pṛthivī śivam antarikṣam dyaur no devy abhayam no astu / śivā diśaḥ pradiśa uddiśo na āpo vidyutaḥ paripāntu sarvataḥ svāhā</s>' (May the earth be at peace, the atmosphere auspicious, may the divine sky bring us fearlessness. May the directions, intermediate directions, and upper directions be auspicious for us; may the waters and lightning protect us on all sides! <s>Svāhā</s>!). '<s>āpo marīcīḥ pravantu no dhiyo dhātā samudro avahantu pāpam / bhūtam bhaviṣyad abhayam viśvam astu me brahma adhiguptaḥ svāra akṣarāṇi svāhā</s>' (May the waters and rays carry forth our prayers; may the Ordainer and ocean carry away evil. May the past and future be fearless; may all be well for me, guarded by <s>Brahman</s>, with the self-radiant syllables! <s>Svāhā</s>!). '<s>viśvādityā vasavaś ca devā rudrā goptāro marutaḥ saṃdantu / ūrjam prajāṃ amṛtaṃ pinvamānaḥ prajāpatir mayi parameṣṭhī dadhātu svāhā</s>' (May all the <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Vasus</s>, gods, <s>Rudras</s>, protectors, and <s>Maruts</s> bestow [blessing]. May <s>Prajāpati</s>, the Supreme, place in me nourishment, offspring, and immortality, swelling [with abundance]! <s>Svāhā</s>!). '<s>Prajāpate na tvad etāny anyaḥ</s>' (O <s>Prajāpati</s>, no other than you [controls] these).
The <s>Sviṣṭakṛt</s> (offering to <s>Agni</s> as maker of good offerings) [is performed] on the eighth [day].
It is prescribed that he should feed <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.
On the following day is the <s>Anvaṣṭakya</s> (supplementary eighth-day rite).

Having set aside [a portion] of that same meat, he should kindle a fire on a slope declining to the south, enclose [the sacrificial ground], make an opening to the north of the enclosure, spread sacrificial grass with its roots, shaking [the grass] three times away from himself, and set out the offerings: rice, <s>kṛsara</s>, <s>pāyasa</s>, curds, <s>manthas</s> (stirred drinks), and honey-<s>manthas</s>.
According to the procedure of the <s>Piṇḍa-pitṛ-yajña</s> (ancestral offering of rice-balls).
Having offered, he should give [offerings] to the ancestors, excluding the honey-mixture.
And to the women, also liquor and sipping-water — this is additional.
Some [prescribe offerings] in pits — in two, or in six.
In the earlier [pits] he should give to the ancestors.
In the later [pits], to the women.
By this [same procedure], the monthly [rite] from [the month of] <s>Māgha</s> through the rainy season, in the dark fortnight of <s>Proṣṭhapadā</s>.
And month by month, in this way, he should establish [offerings] for the ancestors on odd [days].
He should feed nine or fewer [<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>].
Or an odd number.
Even numbers [bring] increase in pure [rites].
Odd numbers in the other [rites].
The circumambulation is to the right; barley [serves] in the place of sesame.
About to mount a chariot, he should touch the two wheels separately with his two hands [saying]: 'I grasp your two front feet; <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s> are your two wheels.'
'The <s>Vāmadevya</s> [<s>Sāman</s>] is the axle' — [this he says] at the axle-base.
He should mount from the right front [saying]: 'I mount you by the virility of <s>Vāyu</s>, by the vigor and sovereignty of <s>Indra</s>.'
He should touch the reins, or [if] without reins, [use] a stick [saying]: 'I hold you by the splendor of <s>Brahman</s>' or 'I hold [you] by Truth (<s>satya</s>).'

When [the horses] begin to move, he should murmur: '<s>sahasrasanim vājam abhivartasva / ratha deva pravaha vanaspate / vīḍvaṅgo hi bhūyāḥ</s>' (Turn toward thousand-fold nourishment! O divine chariot, carry forward, O lord of the forest! For may you be firm-limbed!).
By this [same formula], other wooden vehicles also.
He should touch a part of the chariot [saying]: '<s>sthirau gāvau bhavatām vīḷu prakṣaḥ</s>' (May the two oxen be firm; may the axle be strong).
[For] a boat [he recites]: '<s>sutrāmāṇam pṛthivīm dyām anehasam</s>' (The well-protecting earth and the unassailable heaven).
With a new chariot, having circumambulated clockwise a glorious tree or an unfailing lake, he should bring back fruit-bearing branches.
Or whatever pertains to the household.
He should approach the assembly.
Having murmured '<s>asmākam uttamam kṛdhi</s>' (Make [this] the highest for us) while gazing at the sun, he should dismount.
[Reciting] '<s>ṛṣabham mā samānām</s>' (May I be the bull among my equals) while approaching.
'<s>vayam adya Indrasya proṣṭhāḥ</s>' (Today we are the favorites of <s>Indra</s>) — [this is recited] when the sun is setting.
'<s>tad vo divo duhitaro vibhātīḥ</s>' (O daughters of heaven, you who illuminate) — [this is recited] at dawn.
Now, from here, the examination of the house-site (<s>vāstu parīkṣā</s>).
[Select] ground that is not saline and not disputed.
[Land] having herbs and trees.
In which <s>kuśa</s> grass and <s>vīriṇa</s> grass grow abundantly.
But thorny and milky plants should be dug up with their roots and removed.
<s>Apāmārga</s>, <s>śāka</s>, <s>tilvaka</s>, and <s>parivyādha</s> — these also [should be removed].
Where waters from all sides, meeting in the middle, flowing clockwise around the dwelling-place, would flow to the east silently — that is entirely prosperous.
At the confluence, a dining-hall should be built.
There will be abundant food.
On a slope declining to the right, one should measure out an assembly-hall; it will be free from gambling.
[Otherwise] young men therein become gamblers, quarrelsome, and short-lived.
Where waters flow out in all directions, that [site] is auspicious and free from gambling.
Now, he should examine the house-site with these [tests].
Having dug a pit knee-deep, he should refill it with the same earth.
If there is excess [earth], it is praiseworthy; if level, it is middling; if deficient, it is condemned.
After sunset, he should leave [the pit] filled with water overnight.
If there is water [in the morning], it is praiseworthy; if moist, middling; if dry, condemned.
White [soil], sweet in taste, with abundant sand — [this is best] for a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>.
Red [soil] for a <s>Kṣatriya</s>.
Yellow [soil] for a <s>Vaiśya</s>.
Having ploughed it with a thousand [furrows], he should measure out an even quadrilateral according to the direction.
Or an oblong quadrilateral.
He sprinkles that [site] with a <s>śamī</s> branch or an <s>udumbara</s> (fig-tree) branch, circumambulating thrice clockwise, [reciting] the <s>Śāntātīya</s> [hymn].
And with an unbroken stream of water, [reciting] the three-verse hymn '<s>āpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuvaḥ</s>' (O waters, you are bliss-bestowing).
He should have shelters made in the spaces between the bamboo [framework].
In the pits, he should place lotus stalks and bivalve shells — 'Thereby it [the house] will not be subject to burning' — thus it is known.

Having placed [the materials] in the pit of the central pillar, having spread <s>kuśa</s> grass with tips pointing east and north, he should pour over water mixed with rice and barley [saying]: '<s>acyutāya bhaumāya svāhā</s>' (To the Unshaken, Earthly One, <s>svāhā</s>!).

Then, as it [the pillar] is being raised up, he should consecrate it [with the mantra]: '<s>iha eva tiṣṭha nimitā tilvakāḥ / tām irāvatīm madhye poṣasva / tiṣṭhanti imāḥ tvā prāpann aghāyavaḥ / ā tvā kumāras taruṇa ā vatso jāyatāṃ saha / ā tvā pariśritaḥ kumbha ā dadhnaḥ kalaśair ayan</s>' (Stand right here, O fixed one, [firm] like <s>tilvaka</s> trees! Rich in nourishment, thrive in the midst! These non-enemies have come to you. May young men come to you, may calves be born alongside! May a covered pot come to you, and pots of curds come to you in jars!).
When the ridgepole is being placed,
[he recites]: '<s>ṛtena sthūṇām adhiroha vaṃśa / drāghīya āyuḥ prataram dadhānaḥ</s>' (By cosmic order (<s>ṛta</s>), mount the pillar, O ridgepole, bestowing a longer, more extended lifespan!).
On all four foundation stones, he should place a jewel [saying]: '<s>pṛthivyā adhi sambhava</s>' (Arise from the earth!).

'<s>araṅgaro vāvadīti tredhā baddho varatrayā / irām u ha praśaṃsaty anirām apabādhatām</s>' (The fire-altar speaks, bound threefold with three straps. It praises nourishment and drives away lack of nourishment.) — or [this verse].

Then he should pour water over this [saying]: '<s>aitu rājā Varuṇo revatībhir asmiṃt sthāne tiṣṭhatu modamānaḥ / irāṃ vahanto ghṛtam ukṣamāṇā Mitreṇa sākaṃ saha saṃviśantv</s>' (May King <s>Varuṇa</s> come with the enriching [waters], and abide in this place rejoicing! May they come bearing nourishment, sprinkling with ghee, and settle down together with <s>Mitra</s>!).
Then he pacifies it.
Having placed gold in water mixed with rice and barley, circumambulating thrice clockwise, he sprinkles [reciting] the <s>Śāntātīya</s> [hymn].
And with an unbroken stream of water, [reciting] the three-verse hymn '<s>āpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuvaḥ</s>'.

Having cooked a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (cooked oblation) in the middle of the house, having offered for each verse with the four [verses beginning] '<s>Vāstoṣpate pratijānīhy asmān</s>' (O Lord of the Dwelling, acknowledge us!), having prepared the food and fed <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, he should have them recite: '<s>śivaṃ vāstu, śivaṃ vāstu</s>' (Auspicious be the dwelling! Auspicious be the dwelling!).
The entering of the house (<s>gṛha-prapadana</s>) has been described.
He should enter the house when seeds [are available].
He should plough the field on the later <s>Proṣṭhapadā</s> [<s>nakṣatra</s>], on <s>Phālgunī</s>, or on <s>Rohiṇī</s>.

He should offer — or murmur — for each verse [the hymns beginning]: '<s>kṣetrasya anuvātam</s>' (Following the wind of the field) and '<s>kṣetrasya patinā vayam</s>' (With the lord of the field, we...).
He should consecrate the cows as they are being settled [with the two verses beginning]: '<s>mayobhu vāto abhivātu usrāḥ</s>' (May the wind blow auspiciously for the kine).

[And with]: '<s>āyatīr yāsām ūdhaś caturbilam madhoḥ pūrṇaṃ ghṛtasya ca / tā naḥ santu payasvatīr bahvīr goṣṭhe ghṛtācyaḥ / upa mā etu mayobhuvā ūrjam ca ojaś ca bibhratīḥ / duhānā akṣitam payo mayi goṣṭhe niviśadhvam yathā bhavāmy uttamaḥ</s>' (Those coming, whose udder has four openings, full of honey and ghee — may they be milk-giving for us, many in the cowpen, dripping with ghee! May prosperity come to me, bearing vigor and strength! Milking inexhaustible milk, settle in my cowpen, that I may be the highest!). [And continuing with] '<s>yā deveṣu tanvam airayanta</s>' (Those who displayed their bodies among the gods) and the rest of the hymn (ṚV 10.169.3-4).
Some [prescribe] the <s>Āgāvīya</s> [hymn] (ṚV 6.28).

He should approach the herds [with the formula]: 'O elders among the cows! You are auspicious, you are praised, you are beautiful, you are dear. May I be dear to you! Be at peace with me! Be at peace with me!'
Now, from here, the five [daily] sacrifices (<s>pañca-yajñāḥ</s>).

<s>Devayajña</s> (sacrifice to the gods), <s>bhūtayajña</s> (sacrifice to beings), <s>pitṛyajña</s> (sacrifice to the ancestors), <s>brahmayajña</s> (sacrifice to <s>Brahman</s>), and <s>manuṣyayajña</s> (sacrifice to humans) —

That which one offers into the fire is the <s>devayajña</s>; that which one offers as <s>bali</s> (food offering) is the <s>bhūtayajña</s>; that which one gives to the <s>pitṛs</s> (ancestors) is the <s>pitṛyajña</s>; that which one recites as <s>svādhyāya</s> (self-study) is the <s>brahmayajña</s>; that which one gives to humans is the <s>manuṣyayajña</s>.
One should perform these sacrifices day after day.
Now, the rules of <s>svādhyāya</s> (Vedic self-study).

Going out from the village toward the east or the north, having bathed, in a pure place, wearing the sacred thread in the <s>yajñopavīta</s> manner, having sipped water, with unmoistened garments, having spread out a large covering of <s>darbha</s> grass with tips pointing east, sitting upon them facing east, having arranged the lap, joining the right and left hands together with <s>pavitra</s> (purifying grass) in hand — for it is known: '<s>Darbha</s> grass is the essence of waters and plants; thus one makes the <s>Brahman</s> full of essence.' — gazing at the junction of heaven and earth, or with eyes closed, or in whatever manner one considers oneself composed, thus composed one should recite the <s>svādhyāya</s>.
<s>Om</s>. First the <s>Vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances).
One recites the <s>Sāvitrī</s> thereafter, by half-verses, and the whole — this is the third method.

Then one should recite the <s>svādhyāya</s>: <s>Ṛcas</s> (verses of the <s>Ṛgveda</s>), <s>Yajūṃṣi</s> (formulas of the <s>Yajurveda</s>), <s>Sāmāni</s> (chants of the <s>Sāmaveda</s>), <s>Atharvāṅgirasas</s> (hymns of the <s>Atharvaveda</s>), <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kalpas</s> (ritual manuals), <s>Gāthās</s> (songs), <s>Nārāśaṃsīs</s> (panegyrics), <s>Itihāsa-Purāṇas</s> (epics and ancient lore).

When one recites the <s>Ṛcas</s>, one thereby satisfies the deities with oblations of milk; when the <s>Yajūṃṣi</s>, with oblations of ghee; when the <s>Sāmāni</s>, with oblations of honey; when the <s>Atharvāṅgirasas</s>, with oblations of <s>soma</s>; when the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kalpas</s>, <s>Gāthās</s>, <s>Nārāśaṃsīs</s>, <s>Itihāsa-Purāṇas</s> — with oblations of <s>amṛta</s> (nectar of immortality).

Having recited as much as one considers sufficient, one concludes with this formula: 'Obeisance to <s>Brahman</s>. Obeisance to <s>Agni</s>. Obeisance to the Earth. Obeisance to the plants. Obeisance to Speech. Obeisance to the Lord of Speech. Obeisance to <s>Viṣṇu</s> the Great. I make this offering.'

One satisfies the deities: <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Brahman</s>, the <s>Vedas</s>, the gods, the <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages), all the metres, the syllable <s>Om</s>, the exclamation <s>Vaṣaṭ</s>, the <s>Vyāhṛtis</s>, the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, the sacrifices, Heaven and Earth, the atmosphere, days and nights, numbers, the <s>siddhas</s> (perfected beings), oceans, rivers, mountains, fields, plants, forest trees, <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Apsarases</s>, <s>Nāgas</s>, birds, cattle, <s>Sādhyas</s>, learned ones, <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, beings — ending with these.

Now the <s>ṛṣis</s>: those of the <s>Śatarcin</s> (first <s>maṇḍala</s>), the middle ones, <s>Gṛtsamada</s>, <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, <s>Vāmadeva</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Bharadvāja</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the <s>Pragāthas</s> (authors of the eighth <s>maṇḍala</s>), the <s>Pāvamānīs</s> (ninth <s>maṇḍala</s>), the <s>Kṣudrasūktas</s> and <s>Mahāsūktas</s> (of the tenth <s>maṇḍala</s>).
With the sacred thread in the <s>prācīnāvīta</s> manner (over the right shoulder).

<s>Sumantu</s>, <s>Jaimini</s>, <s>Vaiśampāyana</s>, <s>Paila</s>, the teachers of the <s>Sūtras</s>, <s>Bhāṣyas</s> (commentaries), <s>Bhārata</s>, <s>Mahābhārata</s>, and <s>Dharma</s>; the teachers <s>Jānanti</s>, <s>Bāhavi</s>, <s>Gārgya</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Śākalya</s>, <s>Bābhravya</s>, <s>Māṇḍavya</s>, <s>Māṇḍūkeya</s>; <s>Gārgī Vācaknavī</s>, <s>Vaḍavā Prātītheyī</s>, <s>Sulabhā Maitreyī</s>; <s>Kahola</s>, <s>Kauṣītaka</s>, <s>Mahā-Kauṣītaka</s>, <s>Paiṅgya</s>, <s>Mahā-Paiṅgya</s>, <s>Suyajña</s>, <s>Śāṅkhāyana</s>, <s>Aitareya</s>, <s>Mahā-Aitareya</s>, <s>Śākala</s>, <s>Bāṣkala</s>, <s>Sujātavaktra</s>, <s>Audavāhi</s>, <s>Mahā-Audavāhi</s>, <s>Saujāmi</s>, <s>Śaunaka</s>, <s>Āśvalāyana</s> — and whatever other teachers there are — may they all be satisfied.
Having satisfied the <s>pitṛs</s> (ancestors) for each generation, returning home, whatever one gives — that is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee).
And further it is known: whether standing, walking, sitting, or lying down, whatever sacred text one recites, by that very sacred act one's sacrifice is accomplished.
It is known that there are two occasions for suspending study: when oneself is impure and when the place is impure.
Now, the <s>adhyāya-upākaraṇa</s> (commencement of the Vedic study term).
At the appearance of herbs, on the <s>Śravaṇā</s> (lunar mansion) day of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> (month).
Or on the fifth day, under the <s>Hasta</s> (lunar mansion).

Having offered the <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (shares of clarified butter), one should make <s>ājya</s> oblations to <s>Sāvitrī</s>, to <s>Brahman</s>, to <s>Śraddhā</s> (faith), to <s>Medhā</s> (intelligence), to <s>Prajñā</s> (wisdom), to <s>Dhāraṇā</s> (retention), to <s>Sadaspati</s> (lord of the assembly), to <s>Anumati</s> (divine approval), to the metres, and to the <s>ṛṣis</s>.
Then one offers <s>dadhi-saktus</s> (curds mixed with barley flour).
'<s>Agnim īḍe purohitam</s>' (I praise <s>Agni</s>, the foremost priest) — this is one verse.

'<s>Kuṣumbhakas tad abravīt</s>' (the <s>Kuṣumbhaka</s> bird spoke thus); '<s>āvadaṃs tvaṃ śakune bhadram āvada</s>' (O bird, speak auspicious words); '<s>gṛṇānā jamadagninā</s>' (being praised by <s>Jamadagni</s>); '<s>dhāma te viśvaṃ bhuvanam adhiśritam</s>' (your abode encompasses the entire universe); '<s>gantā no yajñaṃ yajñiyāḥ</s>' (may the sacrificial ones come to our sacrifice); '<s>suśami yo naḥ svo araṇaḥ</s>' (he who is our benevolent companion); '<s>praticakṣva vicakṣva</s>' (look upon, look around); '<s>agne yāhi marutsakhā</s>' (O <s>Agni</s>, come with the <s>Maruts</s> as companions); '<s>yat te rājan śṛtaṃ haviḥ</s>' (O king, whatever cooked oblation is yours) — these are two-verse hymns each.
'<s>Samānī va ākūtiḥ</s>' (May your intention be common) — this is one verse.
'<s>Tat śaṃyor āvṛṇīmahe</s>' (We choose that which brings well-being) — this is one verse.

The one about to begin study, being touched by those who are to study, having offered to these deities, having offered the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (oblation to <s>Agni</s> who makes the offering successful), having eaten <s>dadhi-saktus</s>, then performs the purificatory rite.

To the west of the fire, sitting on <s>darbha</s> grass with tips pointing east, having placed <s>darbha</s> grass in a water vessel, with hands joined in the <s>brahmāñjali</s> (gesture of reverence to <s>Brahman</s>), one should recite.
<s>Om</s>. First the <s>Vyāhṛtis</s> and the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, repeating them three times, one should begin the commencement of the <s>Veda</s>.
Likewise at the <s>utsarga</s> (closing of the study term).
One should study for six months.
Having concluded, one should follow the observance of the <s>brahmāri</s> (celibacy and austerity).
The other observances should be followed in the customary manner.
Some say that a wife should be taken.
That is the <s>Prājāpatya</s> (rite pertaining to <s>Prajāpati</s>).
This is called the annual observance.
On the middle <s>aṣṭakā</s> (eighth day), having offered to these deities with food, they partake of water.
They satisfy these same deities.
And the teachers, the <s>ṛṣis</s>, and the <s>pitṛs</s> (ancestors).
This is the <s>utsarjana</s> (closing ceremony of the study term).
Now, in place of the regular observances, there are optional rites fulfilling specific desires.
One attains those very desires.
Now, for one who is diseased, afflicted, or seized by a wasting illness, a <s>caru</s> (rice oblation) with six offerings.
With the verse '<s>Muñcāmi tvā haviṣā jīvanāya</s>' (I release you with this oblation for the sake of life).

Having seen an unpleasant dream, with the two verses beginning '<s>Adyā no deva Savitar</s>' (O divine <s>Savitṛ</s>, today for us), and with the five verses beginning '<s>Yac ca goṣu duḥsvapnyam</s>' (whatever bad dream occurs among cattle), one should worship the sun.
Or with '<s>Yo me rājan yujyo vā sakhā vā</s>' (whoever is my associate or friend, O king).

After sneezing, after yawning, after seeing something unpleasant, after smelling a foul odor, at the twitching of the eye, or at a ringing in the ear, one should recite: '<s>Sucakṣā aham akṣībhyāṃ bhūyāsam</s>' (May I be of good sight with my eyes), '<s>suvarcā mukhena</s>' (of good radiance with my face), '<s>suśrut karṇābhyām</s>' (of good hearing with my ears), '<s>mayi dakṣa-kratū</s>' (may skill and resolve be in me).'

Having gone to a place one should not have gone, having officiated at a sacrifice for one who should not be sacrificed for, having eaten what should not be eaten, having accepted what should not be accepted, and having struck a sacred tree or sacrificial post — one should offer two <s>ājya</s> (clarified butter) oblations with: '<s>Punar mām aitv indriyam, punar āyuḥ, punar bhagaḥ</s>' (May vitality return to me, may life return, may fortune return), '<s>punar draviṇam aitu mām, punar brāhmaṇam aitu mām, svāhā</s>' (may wealth return to me, may the <s>Brahman</s> return to me, <s>svāhā</s>); '<s>Ime ye dhiṣṇyāso agnayo yathā sthānam iha kalpatām</s>' (May these fires in their stations be arranged here in their proper places), '<s>Vaiśvānaro vāvṛdhāno antar yacchatu me mano hṛdy antaram amṛtasya ketuḥ, svāhā</s>' (<s>Vaiśvānara</s>, having grown strong, may he direct my mind inward, the banner of immortality within the heart, <s>svāhā</s>).
Or with fuel sticks.
Or one may recite silently.

If the sun should set upon one who is unimpaired and sleeping, having observed a vow of silence and sitting down, when night remains, with the five verses beginning '<s>Yena sūrya-jyotiṣā bādhase tamaḥ</s>' (by which solar light you drive away darkness), one should worship the sun as it rises.
If the sun should rise upon one who, though not diseased, has been idle or engaged in improper activity — the same vow of silence applies, and the worship is with the latter four verses.
Wearing the sacred thread, always carrying water, one should worship at the <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight junctions), maintaining silence.
In the evening, facing the northwest, one should recite the <s>Sāvitrī</s> in the eighth direction when the sun-disc is half-set, until the stars become visible.
Likewise in the morning,
facing east, standing, until the sun-disc becomes visible.
If a pigeon should strike the house or fly in, one should offer with the hymn '<s>Devāḥ kapota</s>' (O gods, the pigeon), verse by verse — or one may recite it.
'<s>Vayam u tvā pathaspate</s>' (O <s>Pathaspati</s>, we invoke you) — one should recite this when about to set out on a journey to accomplish a purpose.
'<s>Saṃ Pūṣan viduṣā</s>' (May <s>Pūṣan</s> unite us with one who knows) — when seeking something lost, or when one has gone astray.
'<s>Saṃ Pūṣann adhvanaḥ</s>' (May <s>Pūṣan</s> bring us safely along the path) — when about to undertake a long journey, or a dangerous one.

Now, one who is about to perform the <s>samāvartana</s> (graduation ceremony) should prepare these items: a jewel, a pair of earrings, a pair of garments, an umbrella, a pair of sandals, a staff, a garland, ointment, unguent, collyrium, and a turban — for oneself and for the teacher.
If one cannot obtain both sets, then for the teacher alone.
One should fetch a fuel stick from a tree fit for sacrifice, in the unconquered direction (northeast).
A fresh one, if one desires food; a flourishing one, if one desires nourishment, lustre, or Vedic splendor; one blown upon by the wind, if one desires these.
Both kinds, if one desires both.
Having placed the fuel stick on top, having given a cow and food to <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, one should perform the <s>gaudānika</s> (ceremonial shaving) rite.
One should direct the <s>mantras</s> toward oneself.
With a single razor.

Having bathed with cold and hot water, with the verse '<s>Yuvaṃ vastrāṇi pīvasā vasāthe</s>' (You two wear splendid garments), he should put on a pair of new garments; with '<s>Aśmanas tejo asi cakṣur me pāhi</s>' (You are the lustre of stone; protect my eyes), he should apply collyrium to his eyes.
With '<s>Aśmanas tejo asi śrotraṃ me pāhi</s>' (You are the lustre of stone; protect my ears), he should fasten the earrings.
Having anointed both hands with unguent, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should first anoint the face.
Having extracted the kidneys, one should place them in the hands with the verse 'These two run past the two <s>Sārameya</s> dogs' — the right one in the right hand, the left in the left.
Heart upon heart.
Some also say the testicles.
Some say instead of the kidneys.

Having placed all the limbs according to their proper positions and covered them with the hide, with the verse 'O <s>Agni</s>, do not overturn this cup,' one consecrates the leading forth of the <s>praṇītā</s> (consecrated water).

Bending the left knee, one should offer oblations of <s>ājya</s> (clarified butter) into the southern fire: 'To <s>Agni</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Kāma</s> (desire), <s>svāhā</s>! To the world, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Anumati</s> (divine approval), <s>svāhā</s>!'
The fifth oblation upon the chest of the deceased: 'From you indeed were you born; may he be born again from you. For the heavenly world, <s>svāhā</s>!'
He commands: 'Light the fires simultaneously.'
If the <s>Āhavanīya</s> (offering fire) reaches him first, one should know: 'He has attained the heavenly world.' The son should say: 'He shall prosper there, and this one here.'
If the <s>Gārhapatya</s> (household fire) reaches him first, one should know: 'He has attained the atmospheric world.' The son should say: 'He shall prosper there, and this one here.'
If the <s>Dakṣiṇāgni</s> (southern fire) reaches him first, one should know: 'He has attained the human world.' The son should say: 'He shall prosper there, and this one here.'
If they reach him simultaneously, they declare it to be the highest prosperity.
One consecrates the burning with the verse 'Go forth, go forth by the ancient paths,' and so on.
It is known that one who is burned with this knowledge goes to the heavenly world together with the smoke.

Having dug a knee-deep pit to the northeast of the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire, one should place in it the <s>avakā</s> (aquatic plant) and <s>śīpāla</s>. It is known that from there, having departed, one goes to the heavenly world together with the smoke.
With the verse 'These living ones have separated from the dead,' they return, turning to the left, without looking back.

Reaching a place where there is flowing water, having immersed once, having released a single handful of water, having spoken his <s>gotra</s> (lineage name) and personal name, having come out and put on different garments, having wrung these out once, having released them with the fringes pointing north, they should sit until the stars become visible.
Or they may enter the house when the sun is still visible.
The youngest going first, the eldest going last.
Arriving at the house, they touch a stone, fire, cow-dung, unbroken grain, sesame, and water.
They should not cook food on that night.
They should subsist on purchased or naturally available food.
For three nights they should eat food without alkali and without salt.
For twelve nights, in the case of great elders, they should refrain from gifts and study of the <s>Veda</s>.
Ten days for <s>sapiṇḍas</s> (those within the shared funeral-cake relationship).
And for a teacher who is not a <s>sapiṇḍa</s>.
And for unmarried women.
Three nights for other teachers.
And for a known person who is not a <s>sapiṇḍa</s>.
And for married women.
For a child whose teeth have not yet appeared.
And for a child not yet fully developed.
One day for a fellow student of the <s>Veda</s>.
And for a learned <s>brāhmaṇa</s> from the same village.
The collection of bones should be done after the tenth day, in the dark fortnight, on an odd day, under a single <s>nakṣatra</s> (lunar mansion).
In an unmarked pot — a male in an unmarked one, a female in an unmarked one.
The collectors should be odd in number, not in couples, and advanced in age.
With a mixture of milk and water, walking around three times counter-clockwise with a <s>śamī</s> (Prosopis) branch, one sprinkles with the verse: 'O cool one, you who possess coolness.'
With the thumb and little finger, they should place each bone one by one without making a clinking sound.
The feet first, the head last.

Having carefully collected and arranged them and having filled them with air, in a pit where water would not flow in from any direction except from rain, they should place them with the verse: 'Approach your mother Earth.'
With the next verse, one should scatter earth over them.
After scattering, the next verse.
'I prop you up' — having covered with a potsherd, then returning without looking back and having sipped water, they should offer a <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral offering) for him.
If afflicted by a great calamity or when the moon is waning, on the new-moon day, they should perform a pacification rite.
Before sunrise, the fire together with its ashes and its receptacle should be carried to the south, with the half-verse: 'I send forth the <s>kravyād</s> (flesh-eating) fire far away.'
Having placed it at a crossroads, or where they go around three times counter-clockwise, striking the left thighs with the left hands.

Then, returning without looking back, having sipped water, having shaved the hair of the head, beard, body hair, and nails, they should prepare new pots, jars, water-vessels, garlands of <s>śamī</s> (Prosopis) and flowers, fuel of <s>śamī</s> wood, fire-sticks of <s>śamī</s> wood, and enclosing sticks, a bull's dung, hide, fresh butter, a stone, and as many bundles of <s>kuśa</s> grass as there are young women.
At the time for fire-kindling, one should generate fire with the half-verse: 'Here indeed this other <s>Jātavedas</s> (Fire, knower of beings).'

They should sit keeping the fire lit until late at night, recounting stories of long-lived persons and having auspicious tales narrated — <s>itihāsas</s> (historical narratives) and <s>Purāṇas</s> (ancient legends).

When sounds have ceased or when they have entered the house or dwelling, starting from the right side of the door, one should carry an unbroken stream of water with the verse 'Follow the thread, stretching it, and follow the light of the sky,' up to the northern side.

Then, having piled up the fire and having spread behind it an ox-hide with the neck facing east and the hair upward, he should make the kinsmen mount upon it with: 'Mount up, choosing life and old age.'
'I place this enclosure for the living' — one should place an enclosing stick.

'Placing death within this mountain' — having placed a stone to the north of the fire as a boundary, with the verse 'O death, follow another path,' having offered four oblations, one verse at a time, with 'As the days follow one another in order,' he should look at the kinsmen.

The young women, each separately with their own hands, using fresh <s>darbha</s> (sacred grass) shoots and fresh butter, with the thumb and little finger, should release the eye-ointment with the <s>ājya</s> flowing away from them.
'These women, not widowed, with good husbands' — having applied the ointment, one should look at them.
'She flows with stones — take hold!' — the chief mourner should first touch the stone.
They declare that a tawny bull should be led around.
Then they sit down where they will be comfortable, having covered themselves with an unwashed garment.
They sit without sleeping until sunrise.

After the sun has risen, having recited the <s>Saurya</s> (solar) verses and the <s>svastyayana</s> (benedictory) verses, having prepared the food, having offered into the fire verse by verse with 'Burn away from us the sin that afflicts,' having fed the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, one should have the <s>svastyayana</s> recited.
A cow, a bronze vessel, and an unworn garment are the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (ritual fee).
Now, concerning the <s>pārvaṇa śrāddha</s> (regular ancestral offering), the <s>kāmya</s> (optional), the <s>ābhyudayika</s> (for prosperity), and the <s>ekoddiṣṭa</s> (for a single deceased):

Having seated <s>brāhmaṇas</s> endowed with learning, good conduct, and proper behavior — invited at the proper time, bathed, having cleaned their hands and feet, having sipped water — facing north, seated as one would for the fathers: one for each, or two for each, or three for each.
When they increase, the abundance of fruit increases.
But never one for all.
As many as desired, without restriction.
This is explained in connection with the <s>piṇḍas</s> (funeral cakes).
Having offered water.
Having offered double-bent <s>darbha</s> grass as a seat.
Having offered water.
In three vessels — of metal, stone, and clay — containing the same substance, with <s>darbha</s> grass placed between them, having poured water.

With the verse 'May the divine waters bless us,' when they have been consecrated, one scatters sesame seeds: 'You are the sesame, sacred to <s>Soma</s>, created by the gods at the <s>Gosava</s> sacrifice. Offered by the ancients, with <s>svadhā</s> (hail to the ancestors), gladden the ancestors and these worlds for us. <s>Svadhā</s>, homage!'

With the space between the thumb and the other hand, because of wearing the sacred thread on the left — or with the right hand held by the left: 'O father, this is your <s>arghya</s> (offering of respect). O grandfather, this is your <s>arghya</s>. O great-grandfather, this is your <s>arghya</s>' — in ascending order.
Those who are about to receive them should say, each time: '<s>Svadhā</s>! <s>Arghya</s>!'

After releasing them, one should consecrate with: 'The divine waters that arose on earth, those of the atmosphere and those of the earth, those of golden color, fit for sacrifice — may those waters be pleasant and comforting to us.' Having collected the remainders together, with those waters one who desires sons should anoint his face.
'One should not first remove the vessel in which the <s>arghya</s> has been offered to the ancestors. The ancestors remain seated there' — so said <s>Śaunaka</s>.
At this time, there is the offering of perfume, garlands, incense, lamps, and garments.
Having taken out the food mixed with ghee, one requests permission: 'I shall offer into the fire' — or 'Shall I do it? Shall I perform it?'
The reply of permission: 'Let it be done. Do it. Perform it.'
Then one offers into the fire as stated previously.
Or, upon their permission, into their hands.
'The gods receive offerings through the mouth of fire; the ancestors through the mouth of the hands' — thus says the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> text.
